senses.definition: To cry; to shed tears, especially when accompanied with sobbing or other difficulty speaking, as an expression of emotion such as sadness or joy.

quotes.reference: 1847 November 1, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, Evangeline, a Tale of Acadie, Boston, Mass.: William D. Ticknor & Company, →OCLC, part I:

quotes.text: They weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Numbers 11:13:

senses.definition: To give off moisture in small quantities, e.g. due to condensation.

subsenses.definition: (medicine, of a wound or sore) To produce secretions.
To flow in drops; to run in drops.
examples: a weeping spring, which discharges water slowly

quotes.text: The blood weeps from my heart.
quotes.reference: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]. Epilogue.”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iii]:

senses.definition: To hang the branches, as if in sorrow; to be pendent; to droop; said of a plant or its branches.

quotes.text: The willows weep and the moonbeams sleep / On the mariner's silent grave.
quotes.reference: 1893, Edward William Cole, The best song book in the world, page 314:

senses.definition: (obsolete, transitive) To weep over; to bewail.

quotes.text:
Fair Venus wept the sad disaster
 Of having lost her favorite dove.

[…] Which weep a loss for ever new,
⁠A void where heart on heart reposed;
⁠And, where warm hands have prest and closed,
Silence, till I be silent too.
quotes.reference: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], “Canto XIII”, in In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, page 20:

examples: Sometimes you just have to have a good weep.

quotes.text: He's coming, too, and we both want to mingle our weeps over the wine-cup[.]
quotes.reference: 1897, Bram Stoker, Dracula, New York: Doubleday & McClure, published 1899, page v. 62:

senses.definition: A red or reddish liquid that seeps out from raw muscular meat during storage, consisting mostly of water and protein; "meat juice".
A lapwing; wipe, especially, a northern lapwing (Vanellus vanellus).
